title: Buy Now, Pay Later: Echoes of the 2008 Recession
summary: Long-form explainer compares BNPL's business model and growth to the lead-up to the 2008 subprime mortgage crisis.

assertions.quote: you can defer the cost of any item by splitting the payment into smaller installments over time

verdicts.note: Describes the standard pay-in-4 structure used by Affirm, Klarna, and Afterpay as advertised and generally delivered when payments are kept current.
CFPB: the typical BNPL structure divides a purchase 'into four equal installments,' interest-free, with the first due at checkout and the rest over six weeks.

assertions.quote: access to cheap credit, excessive spending, overextension of subprime borrowers, and unregulated lending standards

verdicts.note: NBER: the largely unregulated nature of the rapidly growing BNPL market is increasingly catching the attention of lawmakers and regulators worried about excess consumption and default risk.

assertions.quote: the loan is funded and issued not by the BNPL company, but instead from a traditional bank that they've partnered with

verdicts.note: Matches disclosed funding structures where banks like Cross River originate the loan and the BNPL company then purchases it from the bank.

assertions.quote: Affirm and other BNPL companies actually lose money on zero interest loans

verdicts.note: Matches Affirm's own disclosed 'loss on loan purchase commitment' line for zero-interest loans.

assertions.quote: Affirm has lost over a billion dollars in the past 4 years
Subprime borrowers as low credit individuals pay the highest interest on loans
